**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, EXCLUSIVITY).**

**What I found.** Section 6.1 (p0037) binds *us*, the Company: we may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products **or** "products substantially similar" (expressly including Wilson's House of Leather / Excelled-type goods), and HDI gets the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand online.

**Why it fails the fallback on material terms:**
- **Duration is open-ended.** It runs "during the term of this Agreement," and Section 4.1 auto-renews annually — so no 12-month cap. Exiting requires 90 days' notice and triggers the Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment (trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000, halved), so the exit is not free.
- **No performance-based release.** There are no service levels and no termination-for-breach right anywhere in the document. The only penalty-free exit (Section 1.6) is a one-time launch-date failure at the outset; after go-live, exclusivity survives regardless of HDI's performance. That is close to the walk-away profile.
- **Scope exceeds a defined category**, reaching competitor-type products generally.

Mitigants noted but not curative: the Section 6.2 closeout carve-out, and HDI's reciprocal two-year covenant in Section 6.3 — which **benefits us and I deliberately left untouched**.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Because HDI is making the build-and-host investment and gives a reciprocal covenant, deletion looked disproportionate, so I drafted to the fallback rather than preferred: narrowed to Deerskin Products, capped at 12 months from the Effective Date, and added automatic release — with no Termination Payment due — on HDI's failure to meet its Article 1 obligations, including the Section 1.6 dates.
